subject: Finovia — sudden p99/throughput spike after v5b quant roll
messages:
From: Tim Hooper <tim.hooper@finovia.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@finovia.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency + errors starting ~07:55 PDT (post-v5b)

Aditya —

We're seeing a sharp jump in p99 latency and an increased 500 rate starting around 07:55 PDT, right after the model upgrade you ran to v5b with the new int8 quant profile. Throughput also dropped ~18% for our hotpath endpoints. Attached are a sampling of request IDs and a zip of traces.

This is impacting customer-facing flows; CX is getting complaints and our SREs have throttled some traffic. Can you confirm if Redwood rolled anything to Finovia's serving pool? We have an active support contract and need an ETA on a fix.

Thanks —
Tim
Head of ML Ops, Finovia

Attachments: p99_traces-20280701.zip, sample_requests_20280701.jsonl

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Tim Hooper <tim.hooper@finovia.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@finovia.com>, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + errors starting ~07:55 PDT (post-v5b)

Tim —

Thanks for the alert and the attachments. We did start a controlled rollout of v5b with the new int8 profile to one of Finovia's dedicated pools at ~07:45 PDT (canary to 10% of capacity). That rollout should not have touched the full pool, but we're treating this as high priority.

I've looped in Irene (inference reliability) and Jordan (deployment lead) to triage. We'll pull traces, check kernel selection and the int8 paths, and either rollback the canary or apply a mitigation ASAP. Expect a status update within 45 minutes.

Apologies for the disruption — we're on it.

— Aditya
Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Attached: Finovia-MAP-v2.docx

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Tim Hooper <tim.hooper@finovia.com>, Lina Park <lina.park@finovia.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + errors starting ~07:55 PDT (post-v5b)

Team —

Initial notes from quick triage: the canary did roll to 10% at 07:45. The traces Tim sent show a consistent p99 tail increase across multiple hosts in the canary pool and an elevated 5xx spike correlated with long kernel compile waits on one host family (A100v3). Error samples are majority internal inference errors (KV cache mismatches causing fallthroughs) not downstream timeouts.

I'm starting a targeted repro against a matching workload with the same sequence lengths and batch distribution. Jordan — can you collect the deployment diffs (quant config and kernel flags) and pause further canaries? Grace — please prepare a hot rollback play and customer-facing note.

We'll update in 30.

—Irene
Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Tim Hooper <tim.hooper@finovia.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + errors starting ~07:55 PDT (post-v5b)

Irene —

Collected diffs: v5b-int8 profile toggles changed per-host kernel selection to enable fused attention kernel v3 and aggressive KV cache eviction at 8MB. Canary trigger was 07:45 and auto-rollout was gated; I have paused all rollouts to Finovia and disabled canary promotion.

I've also pushed a temporary config to force legacy kernel selection for the canary hosts (roll back of the fused kernel only) so we can confirm whether the kernel path is the primary cause. If that does not reduce p99 within two iterations, we will full rollback to v5a.

ETA for first verification after forcing legacy kernels: ~20 minutes.

—Jordan
Deploy Lead, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Tim Hooper <tim.hooper@finovia.com>, Lina Park <lina.park@finovia.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + errors starting ~07:55 PDT (post-v5b)

Tim/Lina —

Quick update: we paused the canary and forced legacy kernel selection on the affected hosts. Early metrics show p99 improving but not fully back to baseline; throughput is recovering ~6% after the change. We're keeping the temporary setting while running more reproductions.

Next steps: 1) full rollback to v5a if we don't get p99 to within 10% of baseline in the next 60 minutes; 2) capture a complete sample of affected requests for postmortem; 3) provide a MAP (mutual action plan) with timeline and credit proposal.

We're committed to a fast remediation. I'll post a final update when we either hit the rollback or confirm stabilization.

—Aditya

From: Tim Hooper <tim.hooper@finovia.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@finovia.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 10:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + errors starting ~07:55 PDT (post-v5b)

Appreciate the fast response. We are keeping throttles on but need to make sure payments flows don't stay degraded for long — that's our highest priority. Please share the MAP and any estimated credit/comp proposal; our CTO will want to know.

Also, can you include any short-term mitigations (e.g., temporary cache sizing or per-route fallback to the lower-capacity model) we can apply from our side immediately?

—Tim

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Tim Hooper <tim.hooper@finovia.com>, Lina Park <lina.park@finovia.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Jul 2028 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + errors starting ~07:55 PDT (post-v5b)

Tim —

Final update for the day: after forcing legacy kernels we saw incremental recovery; however some hosts still experienced p99 variance due to an unexpected interaction between the int8 linear-aliasing optimization and a specific batch-size distribution Finovia sends (many small sequences batched with a single long sequence). We performed a full rollback to v5a at 15:20 PDT and that restored baseline p95/p99 and throughput across all pools. Error rate has stabilized to pre-roll levels.

Attached is the initial MAP (short-term rollback, follow-on root cause analysis, tests to add to gate) and a proposed one-off credit to cover the incident window. Link: https://hub.redwood.ai/deals/DL-7842.

Short-term mitigations you can apply from your side: 1) enable per-route fallback to v4 for highest priority payment flows (we can pre-configure this), 2) reduce max batch aggregation for the hot payment route to avoid the mixed-length batching pattern, 3) temporarily pin to model v5a until we ship a hardened int8 profile.

We'll follow up with an internal postmortem and a plan to reintroduce quantized v5b behind stricter canary gates and additional sequence-length tests. Our VP Sales and Executive Sponsors have been briefed.

We're sorry for the impact — we'll own the follow-through and share the RCA when complete.

—Aditya
Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Finovia-MAP-v2.docx
